summary: This round-2 fix for --audit-plans correctly closes the multi-violation line-shift bug: audit_and_correct_plan_file() now resolves every violation's git-blame/parent-revision lookup in one pass against a single unmutated `lines` snapshot (== HEAD) before any revert is applied, then applies all reverts bottom-to-top so an earlier block's [start,end) range is never invalidated by a later block's line-count change -- this directly fixes the prior REJECT where reverting the first of two violations shifted line numbers and corrupted the second violation's git-blame lookup into a boundary-commit hash. The same pass also adds a 4-value confirm_merge() return (merged, pr_number, merged_at, ambiguous) so a transient `gh` failure is never conflated with a confirmed non-merge and auto-reverted, flags phases with no target_repo as unaudited-coverage warnings instead of silently passing, and persists found-but-uncorrectable violations via an --allow-empty incident commit so they survive process exit. I read the full script and traced the logic (blame/parent resolution happens against the original file before any mutation; bottom-to-top application is provably safe since earlier start indices are never shifted by later mutations), confirmed no other caller in the repo depends on confirm_merge()'s old 3-tuple signature, and actually executed tests/backfill_phase_self_report_test.py rather than trusting the self-report -- all 59 checks across all 11 scenarios pass live, including the new scenario_audit_reverts_two_violations_in_one_file regression test that reproduces this exact prior-round bug. The diff touches only a script, its tests, and an additive incident-log YAML entry; no .github/workflows/** changes, no migration/schema/auth/payment/billing/security path matches, consistent with the pre-classified tier1.
issues: Architectural (pre-existing, not introduced by this diff): REPO_ROOT is a single shared checkout with no locking, so a concurrent --audit-plans/--sweep/--task-id invocation against the same checkout could race. If audit_and_correct_plan_file() writes a revert to disk for one plan file and then crashes before the final commit (e.g. on a later file in the same run), REPO_ROOT is left dirty and sync_repo_root()'s porcelain check will then block every subsequent invocation until a human manually cleans the working tree. Worth a follow-up hardening pass, not a blocker for this fix.
